newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 8.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 8. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The chairman of Indonesia's Nahdlatul Ulama Moslem group, Abdurrahman Wahid, has denied allegations that his recent appearances with leaders from the ruling Golkar party were aimed at deflating the vote of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) in the May 29 general elections.

Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said the removal of Kuntoro Mangkusubroto from his post as the ministry's director-general for mines had nothing to do with his handling of the controversial Busang gold find in East Kalimantan.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, has made it compulsory for joint venture and foreign banks to lend to small businesses.
President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, a business tycoon long considered Indonesia's most eligible bachelor, will marry a descendant of Javanese royalty on April 30.

Credit rating agency Standard and Poor's has assigned a double B-plus corporate credit rating to publicly listed Barito Pacific Timber. The agency said significant liquidity, coupled with modest debt levels, had been a feature of Barito Pacific's operations since its 1993 listing.
